page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running on the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. With one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading overhead, the instance provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB per core. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware AES acceleration.

The hardware configuration includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on remote EBS storage for disk persistence. Network capability is backed by a 133 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Memory throughput benchmarks show high performance, achieving 466.21 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 210.01 GB/sec in write operations, placing memory bandwidth in the top tier. Static web serving throughput measures 113.57 GB/sec, reflecting the network and memory data transfer capacity.

Benchmark results highlight an emphasis on multi-core compute density and memory-bound throughput. Multi-threaded decompression reaches 669.84 GB/sec in bzip3 tests, Clang software compilation scores reach 81,860 in Geekbench, and multi-core Geekbench achieves 25,948. Additionally, Redis key-value workloads reach 133.04 million SET operations per second, and PassMark database operations benchmark in the top tier. Conversely, single-core execution metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier, and small-model LLM generation speeds show lower relative throughput.

The c8gb.16xlarge provides a balanced hardware profile for scaled distributed services that benefit from dedicated physical cores and memory bandwidth without demanding local scratch disks. Primary workload fits include high-throughput web serving, parallel software compilation pipelines, distributed caching systems like Redis, and batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server driven by a 64-core ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 64 dedicated physical cores, 128 GB of memory, and 133 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, it offers a 2 GB per core compute profile. It includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-threaded compilation, memory bandwidth exceeding 466 GB/sec on uncached reads, and 133.04 million Redis operations per second, contrasted with average single-thread performance. The instance fits high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD compilation, and distributed in-memory data processing.
